title: Occupancy map calibration for variant-specific long-context workloads (Llama / Mistral / Qwen)
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
This ticket implements a model-variant occupancy map calibration system that converts empirical batch/sequence length distributions and KV-residency patterns into per-model GPU occupancy lanes used by the allocator and continuous-batching scheduler. The goal is to reduce OOM risk, decrease tail latency for long-context streaming, and regain usable headroom to allow larger effective batch sizes without manual per-deployment tuning.

Why this work matters:
- Existing heuristic memory profiles are conservative for many customers and models, resulting in underutilized GPU headroom and higher cost.
- Long-context variants (32k-64k) produce heterogeneous KV residency across attention layers and variants (Llama / Mistral / Qwen family).
- Continuous batching needs a fast, compact representation of expected occupancy to prevent fragmentation and to decide safe pack sizes for streaming requests.

Scope and deliverables:
1) Data collection pipeline: a lightweight profiler that samples real request traces and synthetic stress cases to produce per-layer occupancy histograms and KV-residency heatmaps for each model variant and quantization profile. Output is a compact occupancy map (serialized CSV/JSON) consumed by the allocator.
2) Calibration algorithm: convert per-layer histograms into discrete occupancy lanes (small, medium, large) with associated eviction thresholds and safe packing heuristics. This will include heuristics for attention-key memory, layer-norm buffers, kv-cache fragmentation, and quantization overhead.
3) Scheduler integration: expose occupancy lanes to the continuous-batching scheduler so packer can prefer same-lane requests and avoid dangerous cross-lane mixing at high GPU utilization.
4) KV cache eviction policy tuning: introduce lane-aware soft-eviction windows to reduce costly full-cache invalidations for streaming token grows.
5) Validation and dashboards: automated benchmarks (worst-case/goldens) + dashboards showing latency P50/P95/P99, OOM incidents, packing efficiency, and cost-per-token changes across models.

Acceptance criteria:
- No increase in production OOM incidents for targeted variants during rollout (canary + staged).
- Packing efficiency increases by >= 8% on 32k/64k workloads in our bench harness (measured as successful token-packs per second at 95th percentile latency target).
- Median latency change < +2% for winning configurations; P99 within SLO budget.
- KV eviction/repopulation events reduced (fewer full-cache flushes) in synthetic growing-window tests.
- Clear documentation (Confluence) of occupancy map format, calibration knobs, and runbook for ops.

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not attempt model-weight-level kernel tuning or quantization algorithm changes (separate research tasks).
- Not modifying public API; all changes are internal to runtime and scheduler.

High-level approach and tradeoffs:
- Conservative lanes are faster to roll out but reduce headroom. We will use a conservative-to-aggressive staged calibration, starting with conservative lane boundaries derived from 99th percentile occupancy and iteratively moving to 95th percentile based on canary health signals.
- Lane granularity: prefer 3 lanes per variant (S/M/L), more lanes increase packing precision but also scheduler complexity. We will prototype with 3 lanes and evaluate diminishing returns.
- Eviction strategy: soft-window eviction avoids immediate KV invalidation but costs memory; we will tune window length by model family and sequence growth rate.

Instrumentation and telemetry required:
- Per-request tag for occupancy-lane decision and pack grouping.
- Counters for lane-cross-pack attempts, pack failures, KV-eviction triggers, and memory fragmentation-triggered defrag events.
- Bench harness measuring packing success rate, per-request latency percentiles, and cost-per-token.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (staging): run occupancy profiler on a 1% traffic shadow for 48h to gather real traces for top 10 customers.
- Phase 2 (canary): enable lane-aware scheduling for 5% of traffic on dedicated capacity nodes with extra telemetry retention. Monitor for 72h.
- Phase 3 (gradual): ramp to 50% over two weeks if metrics within guardrails, otherwise rollback.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: mis-calibrated occupancy lanes cause increased tail latency or subtle pack fragmentation. Mitigation: conservative start, tight canary windows, and automatic rollback triggers.
- Risk: profiler overhead on hot paths. Mitigation: sampling + async aggregation and a low-overhead C++ profiler stub.

Artifacts and links:
- Proto spec (Confluence): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/Occupancy+Map+Spec
- Bench results dashboard (internal): https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/occupancy/variant-bench
- Design doc (Drive): https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/occupancy-calibration
